title: A Painting Seen from Two Distances
title_ja: 二つの距離から見る絵
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在する企業、芸術作品、人物、調査結果ではない。台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A teacher takes a group of art students to an imaginary exhibition.
sentences.ja: 教師が美術の生徒たちを架空の展示に連れていく。

sentences.en: They stop in front of a large painting that contains several groups of colored shapes.
sentences.ja: 複数の色の形が集まった大きな絵の前で立ち止まる。

sentences.en: From a distance, some students describe the painting as a view of a crowded city.
sentences.ja: 遠くから見ると一部の生徒は混雑した都市の景色と記述する。

sentences.en: The teacher asks them to approach the work and examine a small section carefully.
sentences.ja: 教師は作品に近づき小部分を注意深く調べるよう求める。

sentences.en: At close range, the students notice marks that do not look like buildings or people.
sentences.ja: 近距離で生徒は建物や人のようには見えない描線に気づく。

sentences.en: Some marks overlap, and others appear to be separated by tiny areas of unpainted surface.
sentences.ja: 描線の一部は重なり、他は小さな未着色面で隔てられているように見える。

sentences.en: The students discover that individual shapes contribute to an impression that changes when the entire painting becomes visible.
sentences.ja: 個々の形が、絵全体が見えると変化する印象に寄与すると気づく。

sentences.en: They begin to consider how the artist has organized the relationship between the details and the larger composition.
sentences.ja: 作者が細部と大きな構成の関係をどう整理したか考え始める。

sentences.en: The teacher then asks each student to describe the work without immediately identifying the objects represented in it.
sentences.ja: 次に教師は表された物をすぐ特定せず作品を記述するよう各生徒に求める。

sentences.en: One student focuses on the contrast between dark and bright areas, while another describes the rhythm created by repeated shapes.
sentences.ja: 一人は暗部と明部の対比に集中し、別の一人は反復形状が作るリズムを記述する。

sentences.en: Their descriptions help the group notice features that were not apparent when they discussed the picture only as a city scene.
sentences.ja: 記述は都市景観としてのみ絵を議論した時には明らかでなかった特徴に気づく助けとなる。

sentences.en: The class discovers that describing a picture and identifying its subject are not exactly the same activity.
sentences.ja: 絵を記述することと主題を特定することは完全に同じ活動ではないと気づく。

sentences.en: Before leaving, the students return to their original viewing position.
sentences.ja: 帰る前に生徒は元の鑑賞位置に戻る。

sentences.en: They can still recognize the city, but they now pay greater attention to the way its appearance has been constructed.
sentences.ja: 都市を認識できるが、今度はその外見がどう構成されたかにより多く注意を払う。

sentences.en: Their understanding has developed through movement between two different ways of observing the same work.
sentences.ja: 理解は同一作品の二つの異なる観察方法を行き来することで発展した。

sentences.en: The fictional lesson offers no definite interpretation of an actual painting.
sentences.ja: 架空授業は実在の絵の確定的解釈を示すものではない。

sentences.en: Artistic understanding can develop when viewers move between details and the whole work.
sentences.ja: 鑑賞者が細部と作品全体を行き来すると芸術理解が発展し得る。

sentences.en: A change in viewing distance may make certain relationships easier to recognize.
sentences.ja: 鑑賞距離の変化は特定の関係を認識しやすくするかもしれない。

sentences.en: Looking closely does not necessarily replace an initial impression but may help people explain how that impression was created.
sentences.ja: 近くで見ることは当初印象を必ずしも置き換えず、印象がどう作られたか説明する助けになるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The students have learned to ask not only what a painting shows but how it shows it.
sentences.ja: 生徒は絵が何を示すかだけでなくどう示すか問うことを学んだ。

vocabulary.definition: way parts of a work are combined
repeated pattern of movement or sound
in a way that must occur

questions.prompt: What do students see from a distance?
What does the teacher ask them to do?
options: Approach and examine a small section.

questions.prompt: Why do individual marks look different close up?
options: Their combined effect differs from their separate appearance.
The painting changes physically when approached.
The students see a completely different work.
Every mark clearly represents a building.
The artist's age and the museum's location.
The cost of paint and the size of the room.

questions.prompt: What does one student focus on?
options: Contrast between dark and bright areas.
It makes the original subject impossible to recognize.
It requires students to agree on one interpretation.
It helps reveal other features of the painting.

questions.prompt: What happens when they return to their original position?
options: They no longer see a city.
They recognize the city and notice how it was constructed.
They are unable to describe any shapes.
Moving between different ways of observing.
Standing in one place the whole time.
A painting can only be understood from a distance.
Looking at details and the whole can reveal how artistic impressions are created.
Identifying objects is the only goal of art observation.
Every viewer must experience an identical impression.

grammar.focus: when the entire painting becomes visible
not only what a painting shows but how it shows it
grammar.explanation_ja: not only A but Bの並列、間接疑問。

paraphrases.source: They stop in front of a large painting that contains several groups of colored shapes.
paraphrases.rewrite: The large painting is made up of groups of colored shapes.

paraphrases.source: The students discover that individual shapes contribute to an impression that changes when the entire painting becomes visible.
paraphrases.rewrite: The combined impression appears when people can see the whole work.

paraphrases.source: The teacher then asks each student to describe the work without immediately identifying the objects represented in it.
paraphrases.rewrite: The teacher asks for a description before students name the depicted objects.

paraphrases.source: The students have learned to ask not only what a painting shows but how it shows it.
paraphrases.rewrite: Students learn to consider both a painting's subject and its method of presentation.
